description: Five Rust crates for orchestration and dependency discipline: lgwks_bot's script! language for bounded, tenant-keyed async flows; lgwks_std primitives; lgwks_ast parsers; lgwks_deps the audited dependency storefront.
rules: The supported surfaces are script!, try_join! and lgwks_bot::script; lgwks_ast's documented parser and scan module; and lgwks_deps's gate and storefront module. Every other item is support code with no compatibility promise.
The lgwks_deps gate is check_dependencies/check_verdict returning Verdict, Refusal and GateError; lgwks_ast::scan::scan_path runs the five defect detectors through the same checked parse.
Use lgwks_ast::Language::of_path or of_shebang, then try_parse and inspect_ast; a refused source is reported through ParseError::to_diagnostic, never treated as clean.

Write orchestration as a script! block, not as hand-rolled spawn, sleep and retry loops. Each block is one bounded primitive: fan-out, deadline, retry, overlap, named step, readiness and admitted plan.

Fan out with `each x in xs, at most N at once:`, bound a wait with `within 2s:`, retry with `retry up to 3 times, waiting 100ms:`, overlap branches with `together:`, and name a step with `step name:`.

Every flow takes a Scope first. The scope carries the tenant, the step path and the cancellation token, and a step key hashes tenant, run and structural path, so two runs of one flow never share a key.
Inside a retry the key is identical on every attempt, so an effect keyed by it happens once. Work that is one act across runs names itself with Scope::business_key, which stays run-free.

A host's runs share one retry budget: the reserve is 10, credit above it is earned by first attempts, expires after ten seconds without one and never pools past twice the reserve; a refused run is Throttled.

A script! block also emits a constant ARCHITECTURE: the flows it declares and the tree of blocks inside, with bounds, deadlines and retry budgets. Read or diff that instead of re-deriving the orchestration.

`lgwks-ast script diff <base> <head> [--json]` classifies the architecture change between two checked-out source roots; it exits 1 on a widening with no `// lgwks-architecture-approved: <reason>` line in the head.

Untrusted model or tool output enters a run only through admit, which returns a typed Plan or a typed FlowError carrying the provenance of the refused bytes. Do not parse model output and act on it directly.

A flow fails with a FlowError that names the step path. Retry is decided by the variant, never by the message: FlowError::is_retryable is the only rule retry reads. Match the variant; never parse an error string.

lgwks_bot::keyed keeps one effect per caller key on a receiver with no idempotency key: read, wait out the in-flight bound, read again, create once, and reconcile a lost create answer by read-back. gh::issue is its adapter.
lgwks_macros is the proc-macro crate behind script!. It depends on lgwks_ast, which owns the one parser for the language (lgwks_ast::script::parse) and the one refusal vocabulary.

lgwks_bot enables script! through its default `script` feature. Its other features (io, net, process, fs, signal, inspect, ephemeral, profile) are off by default; --no-default-features withdraws the runtime surface.

Prefer lgwks_std over a third-party crate for encoding, fs traversal, glob, hex, hashing, JSON, RON, regex, retry budgets, timestamps, UUIDs, HTTP and tracing; each is a Cargo feature, the default `standard` set carries all of them but http, and `full` adds http.

Use lgwks_std::trace for diagnostics. Applications call install_default once at the process edge; libraries emit structured events and return typed errors, and do not unwrap or expect on recoverable paths.
Every third-party engine (tokio, bevy, gpui, appcui, candle, tokenizers) is a default-off lgwks_deps feature reached through lgwks_deps::storefront.
The lgwks-deps CLI audits a repository against contract/APPROVED.toml, and check_verdict is the same verdict as a library call.

Licences differ by crate: lgwks_bot is MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft), while lgwks_std, lgwks_ast, lgwks_deps and lgwks_macros are Apache-2.0. The LICENSE file in a crate's directory governs that crate.
A release is uploaded before it is tagged, and after the last tag `cargo run -p lgwks_deps --bin published-consumer` builds every published crate from crates.io at its newest tag.
